## Gateway 503 Incident — On-Call Handoff

**Root cause:** Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, author a.novak, 2026-03-14T02:12–02:14Z) shipped config change `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` ("connection-per-request for pool isolation"). This made every request claim its own DB connection instead of sharing the pool. Pool size stayed fixed at 20, so it saturated within ~33s of the config applying.

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14T02:14:18Z (first 503, `req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc`) through end of available log excerpt — ongoing at last log line reviewed. First warning sign at 02:14:14Z (`acquire slow: waited 100ms`). Errors hit all upstreams (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc) — confirms shared gateway pool, not one bad backend. `/health` unaffected (separate pool). Exact error:
```
ERROR pool req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```
Waiting-queue count climbed steadily (13→19+), never drained.

**Scope check:** Workers (`logs/worker.log`) unaffected — no 503s, no pool errors in the same window. Jobs completed normally with low db_wait. Workers use a separate DB pool from the gateway's request pool, so blast radius is gateway-only.

**Rollback target:** `dep-4471` (gateway, config gen 119). Revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`, or if per-request isolation is required, raise pool size to match new demand before re-applying.

**Not implicated:** dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) both shipped after the 503s started — unrelated, no rollback needed.
